items.title: 53566_Benjamin F.
items.q: I had the music store, and I wanted some records by Kid Ory because he was very popular, and he made the records

ctx.x: Oh. 'Cause I understood from what I read that Kid Ory was on the record but the...it was...you...you were the leader, and it was under the name of your band.

No, I was just the promoter. Kid Ory... I had the music store, and I wanted some records by Kid Ory because he was very popular, and he made the records, and it is Kid Ory's band but they called it the uh, I think, the...some of the records had on it "Reb Spikes' Pods of Pepper" but my other band...I had another little band that I called Reb Spikes' Pods of Pepper. His was called the Kid Ory's Creole Band.
I see, and that was what was supposed to be on the record.

items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: And then they asked me to record for them.

ctx.x: You mean with that? For the Spikes Brothers. And the Nordscocks. You do to us.

Oh, after I started playing, I told you, I sent you for my band. Yeah. And I got a Spikes Brothers. The book was the saxophone play, you know. Yeah. One play to take home. And so they opened a music store in Los Angeles. And then they asked me to record for them. Where were you? Well, when they asked me to record, I was here in Oakland. I was working in Oakland at Creole Cafe in Ferdinand Wood. And so I went down on, after engaging with them, I went down. No, I made a special trick. Go down and record for them.
You took the whole band with you? Mm-hmm. Went on the train?

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: So I went to Spikes, Rip Spikes. And I said, Rip, what happened to the master record, the Sunshine Label? I recorded it.

ctx.x: Yeah, those are hard to find.

And when it started going up, I heard about it. It was selling for $35 and kept going up. So I went to Spikes, Rip Spikes. And I said, Rip, what happened to the master record, the Sunshine Label? I recorded it. You want to sell them? I haven't got them. He said, well, we sold the house and we left them in the garage and the people threw them in the alley. And then when I told him what happened, how the record was selling, you know, what people were getting for them, boy, he didn't know what to say. But I wasn't…
